land.text: the whole Republic of China of Cliopatria's 1914-1915 shape, turned into a monarchy

predecessors.note: Yuan Shikai was proclaimed 'Great Emperor of the Chinese Empire' on 12 December 1915; the accession rites were put off to 1 January 1916, the start of 'Hongxian Year 1'. The dossier starts in 1916 so that the Republic and the Empire are not drawn together in 1915.

land.text: the whole of the empire's land less the provinces that had declared independence; 'the Republic of China was restored' on 23 March 1916 under Yuan, then Li Yuanhong from 6 June

successors.note: Yuan abandoned the monarchy on 22 March 1916; the Hongxian year was abolished on 23 March.

keyframe_review.note: 8,439,386 km2: the whole Republic of China's claim (the same outline as the 1914-1915 Republic, which sits next to the Great Mongol State and Tibet rather than containing them). The infobox gives no area. Yunnan declared independence on 25 December 1915 (National Protection War page), Guizhou and Guangxi 'between January and March 1916', so the Empire held a smaller land than the shape; the other provinces named in the page ('Guangdong, Shandong, Hunan, Shanxi, Jiangxi and Jiangsu followed suit ... shortly thereafter') are undated. Cliopatria also keeps the row for all of 1916 though the monarchy ended on 22 March. [fx-08 2026-11-01: the Cliopatria outline holds about 1,240 cells of Tibet's land (Chamdo, western Kham, the Tawang tract), so it does not 'sit next to' Tibet as said above; the tibet dossier draws these cells and the compiler gave them to Tibet by the size rule in 1916. Subtracted here and in /ledger/0. Tibet (1912-1951) page: 'Since 1912, Tibet had been de facto independent of Chinese control'; the page names no holder of Chamdo before 1918 ('In 1918, Lhasa regained control of Chamdo and western Kham'), which the republic-of-china ledger (/ledger/4, /ledger/9) reads as Chinese occupation of Tibetan land.]

region.text: the Republic of China's land, now the Empire: the Beiyang government at Beijing, without Tibet's land

ledger.note: 1916: Yuan Shikai becomes emperor of China. An assembly elected him emperor on 11 December 1915; he was proclaimed 'Great Emperor of the Chinese Empire' on 12 December 1915 and delayed the accession rites until 1 January 1916, 'Hongxian Year 1'. [fx-08 2026-11-01: Tibet's land is left out of the founding region: 'Since 1912, Tibet had been de facto independent of Chinese control' (Tibet (1912-1951) page).]
1916: Yunnan is gone before the Empire begins. 'Cai E and Tang Jiyao declared independence in Kunming. The date was 25 December 1915', and the National Protection Army marched out of it.
1916: Guizhou and Guangxi declare independence. They 'declared their independence between January' and 'March 1916'; the page gives no day, so the month is the end of that window.

region.text: the whole Empire, Beijing and the provinces still loyal, passing back to the Republic of China

ledger.note: 1916: Yuan Shikai gives up the throne on 22 March, 83 days into the reign. 'Yuan deliberated with Liang Shiyi on 17 March and abandoned the monarchy on 22 March'; the Hongxian year was abolished on 23 March and the Republic of China restored. The National Protection War went on until 14 July 1916 (second page); Yuan died on 6 June.

wars.name: National Protection War

zones.text: Yunnan, the base of the uprising
Sichuan, where Yuan's troops 'suffered a major defeat'

wars.outcome: Yuan's defeat: the monarchy was abandoned on 22 March 1916, Yuan died on 6 June and the war was ended on 14 July 1916; the seceded provinces came under local warlords.
wars.note: Began with the Yunnan declaration of 25 December 1915; the page lists Guangdong, Shandong, Hunan, Shanxi, Jiangxi and Jiangsu as declaring independence 'shortly thereafter', undated.

certainty.note: The empire's limits are the provinces of the Republic (administrative lines); the frontiers with Tibet and Outer Mongolia, which the pages do not treat, are not sharp.

notes: Page budget (2) spent on the article and the National Protection War. Same state as republic-of-china in every sense but the title: the Wikipedia article says 'the Republic of China was restored'; the colour agent should give the Empire the Republic's colour (or fold it into republic-of-china as a rename); the dossier is kept separate because Cliopatria has its own row (Q175379) and the brief assigns it. Cliopatria's single 1916 shape covers all of 1916, but the monarchy lasted 1 January to 22 March: the rest of 1916 (23 March on) belongs to republic-of-china (see its new keyframe). The seceding provinces went to the National Protection Army and then to provincial warlords (Yunnan, Guangxi cliques): no dossiers exist for them; the warlord cliques are the ea-08-x batch's job. The undated secessions (Guangdong, Shandong, Hunan, Shanxi, Jiangxi, Jiangsu) are not in the ledger because the page gives no dates and does not say they fell inside the 83 days.
